title_original: Bedford Park Trailer: Stephanie Ahn’s Sundance Winner Captures an Unexpected Relationship

blocks.text: Winner of the U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Debut Feature at the Sundance Film Festival earlier this year, Stephanie Ahn’s Bedford Park is now gearing up for a qualifying run ahead of a release next spring. The drama, following a Korean American woman finding an unexpected connection with a man responsible for a car accident involving her mother, stars Moon Choi, Son Suk-ku, Won Mi Kyung, Kim Eung Soo, and Jefferson White. Ahead of a qualifying run on December 11 in NY and LA and nationwide release on March 5, 2027 from Sony Pictures Classics, the first trailer and poster have arrived.

Here’s the synopsis: “Audrey is a 36-year-old physical therapist caught between her distinctly American identity and her loyalty to her Korean immigrant family. When she meets Eli, a Korean-American with a fractured past, they journey through an unexpected relationship that starts as friends and goes on to become a love story that transcends the cultural pressures each of them face – and which lifts them up and helps define them.”

“To be honest, these are some of my most challenging scenes as an actor,” Moon Choi told us at Busan International Film Festival . “Looking back at my career, I did have some dark or heavily emotional scenes in the past, but what Audrey’s going through in this movie is pretty dark, especially in the beginning. But I don’t really think about it in those terms. I just thought that this is something she is placed into abruptly. Something that she has to go through moment to moment. I didn’t necessarily think: How should I approach this? Should I approach it in a different way from the lighter scenes? I just tried to focus on what she’s actually going through physically and mentally step by step. It was challenging, but I wasn’t uncomfortable about it.”
